name: ATtiny84
description: 14-pin 8-bit AVR microcontroller with 8 KB flash, 512 B SRAM and 512 B EEPROM, offering 12 GPIO in a breadboard-friendly DIP-14. Compared to the ATtiny85 it trades the high-speed PLL for more I/O and an 8-channel 10-bit ADC, plus a USI for SPI/I2C. Used when a project needs more pins than a tiny85 but should stay small, cheap and Arduino-programmable. Standout trait: generous I/O and ADC count in a sub-$2 14-pin DIP.

typical_application: Mid-pin-count sensor nodes and controllers needing several ADC inputs and PWM outputs in a small DIP-14 footprint.
gotchas: PB3/pin 4 is the RESET pin; reclaiming it as GPIO disables ISP and needs a high-voltage programmer to undo
pin 1 is VCC and pin 14 is GND, the opposite end-arrangement from many DIP MCUs, so it is easy to wire backwards
no hardware UART; serial is via USI or software
ships with CKDIV8 fuse set, so the internal oscillator starts at 1 MHz until reconfigured
port pins split across PORTA (8) and PORTB (4); Arduino core pin numbers do not match physical pin order
plain (non-V) grade is not rated for full-speed operation below 2.7 V
